title: Integrate mixed-workload scenarios into perf-canary (nightly) + alerting + Slack routing
creator: Lena Fischer
project: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
- Add mixed-workload benchmark scenarios to perf-canary as a nightly job across representative SKUs/regions.
- Alert on tail latency regressions (p95/p99, TTFT) and meaningful throughput regressions.
- Route notifications to #eng-runtime and #eng-sre with actionable context (scenario, model, SKU, runtime build, delta vs baseline, links to dashboards/logs).

Context
- Mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) have caused head-of-line blocking and p95 tail latency spikes.
- We are adding a short/long prompt-aware scheduler policy behind a flag; perf-canary needs a stable, automated signal to catch regressions while iterating on policy knobs and kernel selection stability.

Scope
- perf-canary:
  - Define a new nightly job group for mixed-workload scenarios (e.g., 80/20 short/long, 50/50, long-spike).
  - Pin a baseline build (runtime-1.18 baseline tag) for comparisons; support explicit override for candidate builds.
  - Export results to the existing perf-canary reporting sink (Grafana/metrics store) with consistent naming.
  - Implement alert rules and Slack notifications with clear rollback guidance.

Scenarios (initial)
- mix_80_20: 80% short prompts (chat-like), 20% long-context prompts.
- mix_50_50: equal mix.
- long_spike: periodic bursts of long-context requests on top of steady short traffic.

Models / SKUs / regions (initial set)
- Models: Redwood-verified open instruct model(s) used in scheduler prototype bench plan (align with benchmark-lab scenarios).
- SKUs: one primary hosted SKU and one dedicated-like SKU (representative GPU pool).
- Regions: start with us-east; optional follow-up to add eu-west after noise analysis.

Metrics tracked (pass/fail inputs)
- TTFT p50/p95 (overall + per-class if available)
- E2E latency p50/p95/p99 (overall)
- Queue time p50/p95 (if emitted in perf run)
- Throughput (tokens/sec or req/sec, consistent with perf-canary harness)
- Error rate (non-2xx / generation failures)

Alert thresholds (initial; tuned with SRE)
- Hard fail / page-to-#eng-sre:
  - p95 E2E latency regression >= +15% vs baseline on mix_80_20 for 2 consecutive runs, OR
  - TTFT p95 regression >= +20% vs baseline for 2 consecutive runs, OR
  - Error rate >= 0.5% (sustained within run) where baseline is < 0.1%.
- Soft fail / notify-to-#eng-runtime:
  - p95 regression >= +10% (single run) OR
  - throughput regression <= -7% vs baseline (single run).
- Always include: absolute numbers, % delta, run ID, runtime SHA/tag, SKU, region, and links.

Slack routing
- #eng-runtime: all soft-fail and hard-fail notifications.
- #eng-sre: hard-fail notifications only (aligned with tail-latency SLO guardrails during canary).

Acceptance criteria
- A nightly perf-canary job executes mixed-workload scenarios and publishes results.
- Alerts trigger reliably (tested by forced regression or threshold manipulation in a staging branch).
- Messages include enough context to triage without opening the codebase (scenario + delta + links).
- Noise level is acceptable (<= 1 false positive/week after initial tuning; follow-up issue if not).

References / links
- Benchmark plan (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/mixed-workload-benchmark-plan.json
- Dashboard spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/scheduler-class-metrics-dashboard-spec.json
- SLO guardrails (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json
- perf-canary implementation PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-611-runtime-scheduler-canary-job.json
- benchmark-lab scenarios PR (dependency): sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-903-add-mixed-workload-scenarios.json
comments: 2025-12-03 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted job spec for perf-canary. Plan is to reuse benchmark-lab scenario definitions (mix_80_20, mix_50_50, long_spike) to avoid divergence. Need final call from SRE on thresholds + whether #eng-sre gets all notifications or only paging-class ones.

2025-12-05 (Aisha Bello): Prefer routing only hard-fail to #eng-sre. For hard-fail, include recommended next step: (1) rerun to confirm, (2) check Grafana panel for latency breakdown, (3) if confirmed and on candidate build -> block promote; if on main -> file incident per runbook.
2025-12-09 (Rina Kobayashi): benchmark-lab PR-903 merged; scenario names finalized. Please keep perf-canary naming identical so reports join cleanly: scenario_id={mix_80_20,mix_50_50,long_spike}.

2025-12-12 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented nightly job in perf-canary (PR-611). Added baseline pinning via PERF_BASELINE_TAG and candidate via PERF_CANDIDATE_TAG. Outputs include runtime tag/SHA and hardware profile. Working through alert rule tuning; first dry run shows ~6-8% variance on throughput depending on time of day.

2025-12-16 (Sean Gallagher): Throughput variance is expected. For now, avoid paging on throughput-only deltas; keep as notify-only unless paired with latency regression. Also require 2 consecutive runs for hard-fail to reduce noise. Approved proceeding.

2025-12-19 (Sahana Iyer): Added 2-consecutive-run gating for hard-fail alerts; soft-fail stays single-run notify. Slack messages now include: scenario, model, sku, region, baseline vs candidate, p95/TTFT deltas, and direct link to perf-canary run details + Grafana dashboard. Requesting final review from Allison on metric names so dashboards auto-link correctly.

2025-12-20 (Allison Grant): Metric names look consistent with existing perf-canary conventions. Please include the dashboard UID in the Slack message (not just a generic link) so it lands on the pre-filtered view. Otherwise approved.

2026-01-10 (Sahana Iyer): Marking done. Nightly job running in us-east on two SKUs. Alerts wired: #eng-runtime receives all; #eng-sre receives hard-fail only. Added runbook snippet to the perf-canary README in PR-611 notes. Follow-up recommended: add eu-west once we have 2 weeks of baseline variance data.
